One page, in order, from nothing to a working skill in Claude Code. Steps 1–4 are the setup.
Steps 5–10 add optional companions; each links to its own guide.

## 1. Prerequisites

| Need | Check | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude --version` | Runs the skill |
| Python 3 | `python3 --version` | The skill's scripts (standard library only, no `pip install`) |
| git | `git --version` | Install and update the skill |
| A Higgsfield account | [higgsfield.ai](https://higgsfield.ai) | Only to generate from the agent (step 4) |

## 2. Install the skill

Personal install (available in every project):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OSideMedia/higgsfield-ai-prompt-skill ~/.claude/skills/higgsfield
```

Project install (only in one project, shared with its collaborators):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OSideMedia/higgsfield-ai-prompt-skill .claude/skills/higgsfield
```

Claude Code registers the root `SKILL.md` as one skill, `higgsfield`. The 35 sub-skills under
`skills/` are opened from there by path; they are not separate skills.

Update later with `git -C ~/.claude/skills/higgsfield pull`. Your memory and ledger live outside
the skill folder (step 3), so an update or reinstall keeps them.

## 3. Check it works

From the skill folder:

```bash
cd ~/.claude/skills/higgsfield
python3 scripts/higgsfield_memory.py where    # memory folder: ~/.higgsfield-skill/db/
python3 scripts/higgsfield_memory.py health   # "issues": [] means the memory is sound
```

Then start `claude` in any project and ask for a prompt, for example *"Give me a Kling prompt for
a slow push-in on a rainy neon street"*. The skill should pick it up without being named. If it
does not, ask Claude *"which skills do you have?"* and check `higgsfield` is listed. If it is missing, the
clone is in the wrong place: the folder must sit directly in `.claude/skills/`.

Your documents and deliverables go in a `workspace/` folder (`input/`, `output/`,
`processed/`) in the project you are working in, created on first use.

## 4. Connect Higgsfield (optional, to generate from the agent)

Without this step the skill writes prompts and you paste them into higgsfield.ai. To have the
agent generate too, install the Higgsfield CLI; in a terminal agent it is preferred over the MCP:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/higgsfield-ai/cli/main/install.sh | sh
#   or: brew install higgsfield-ai/tap/higgsfield
higgsfield auth login
```

Before spending credits on a planned generation, the free preflight checks it against the
platform's enums and rules:

```bash
python3 scripts/preflight.py --model <id> --param K=V --strict
```

The MCP connector (`https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp`) and Higgsfield's bundled skills are covered
in README → Higgsfield Stack Integration; how they share work with this skill is in
`skills/higgsfield-stack/SKILL.md`.

## 5. Superpowers (optional): planning and dev workflows

```text
/plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
```

Brainstorming, planning and code work come from Superpowers; every Higgsfield prompt still
comes from this skill under its HARD RULES. See [`superpowers.md`](superpowers.md).

## 6. claude-mem (optional): memory across sessions

```bash
npx claude-mem install
```

Session continuity comes from claude-mem; filter triggers, prompt failures and the generation
ledger stay in the skill's own memory, which is the record. Wrap client briefs and keys in
`<private>` tags. See [`claude-mem.md`](claude-mem.md).

## 7. OmniRoute (optional): route the agent's LLM calls

```bash
npm install -g omniroute && omniroute
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:20128"     # root URL, not …/v1
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="<your OmniRoute key>"
claude
```

This changes the model that writes prompts, not the Higgsfield model that renders them. Small
models miss more rules: keep the preflight in step 4. See [`omniroute.md`](omniroute.md).

## 8. Caveman (optional): fewer tokens in the agent's chat

```bash
npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman -g
```

Fine for the agent's explanations; never for the prompt itself or the skill's own files. Ask for
each prompt in a code block, and never run `/caveman-compress` on the skill. See
[`caveman.md`](caveman.md).

## 9. Claude Security (optional): scan the skill's code

```text
/plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official
/claude-security scan scripts/ and .github/workflows/
```

Anthropic's vulnerability scanner. Use it to check the scripts the skill runs on your machine,
or a branch before a PR. It does not touch prompt writing. See
[`claude-security.md`](claude-security.md).

## 10. ccusage (optional): see what Claude Code costs

```bash
npx ccusage@latest claude daily --instances
```

Claude token usage and estimated cost by day and project, plus an optional status line. It
tracks the writing cost only; Higgsfield credits stay in the skill's ledger
(`higgsfield_memory.py ratio <project> --credits`). See [`ccusage.md`](ccusage.md).

## Quick reference

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Update the skill | `git -C ~/.claude/skills/higgsfield pull` |
| Where is my memory? | `python3 scripts/higgsfield_memory.py where` |
| Memory stats | `python3 scripts/higgsfield_memory.py stats` |
| Preflight a generation | `python3 scripts/preflight.py --model <id> … --strict` |
| Lint a Seedance prompt | `python3 scripts/seedance_lint.py "<prompt>"` (or `--file prompt.txt`) |
| Log a generation | `python3 scripts/higgsfield_memory.py log-gen <project> --model X --tags a,b --outcome kept` |
